newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude oil ends down, fundamentals weak.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude oil ends down, fundamentals weak.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil made further downside on Monday in a market led by weak fundamentals, brokers said.

Most weakness was seen on the front end with April Brent crude closing down some 58 cents at $19.27 a barrel. May Brent lost just 52 cents to trade at $19.15 at the close as the April/May spread narrowed from an opening 20 cents to around 7-10 cents by the end of the day.

"Fundamental weakness on the crudes is leading this market. The sell off was led by WTI (crude). No-body wants crude oil. If anything they are cutting (refinery) runs because you can't make money in this market," one broker commented.
"There's no point in looking at support levels in a market so strongly led by fundamentals," another said.
U.S. products, which had held relatively strongly for much of the day lost substantial ground near the close and brokers said this did not bode well for Tuesday's opening.
"The products were holding well and were smashed near the end. It's not a good sign for tomorrow," one commented.
March gas oil closed earlier down just two dollars at $167 a tonne but brokers said the late losses on crude and NYMEX products would slash another few dollars off IPE gas oil on Tuesday.

Refinery margins in North West Europe saw only gasoline as supportive and on Monday simple refineries were losing money on every barrel they processed. Many refiners had cut refinery throughput and others were considering cuts.
On the physical market benchmark Brent crude oil traded substantially lower on Monday with three cargoes moving at April Brent -35 cents - down from a deal on Friday at April Brent -24 cents.
U.S. markets were similarly oversupplied as the focus of U.S. refinery maintanance moves to the midcontinent from the U.S. Gulf Coast.
